title: VPC handoff playbook for regulated tenants (lite) - draft
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, operational-first runbook aimed at onboarding highly regulated customers into a minimal viable VPC footprint for Redwood Private. The intent is to reduce handoff time by focusing on the smallest safe set of deliverables we need to get a customer into a working, audited state. This doc is intentionally 'lite' — it assumes the reader will follow deeper reference patterns after initial handoff.

Assumptions:
- Customer requires network isolation + encrypted egress control (company/regulatory requirement).
- We are deploying Redwood Private components into a customer-managed VPC (GCP/AWS/Azure) or an air-gapped datacenter.
- Customer provides a CIDR range and at least one NAT/bastion host subnet.
- Customer will accept a restricted IP allowlist for control-plane connectivity or a dedicated secure tunnel (recommended for regulated).

High-level architecture (textual):
- Management plane (Redwood control plane): hosted or customer-remote; communicates to customer VPC via mTLS tunnel or static allowlist.
- Data plane (in-customer): inference nodes (GPU pool), internal service mesh (lightweight), optional ingress proxy and egress gateway.
- Bastion/Jump host in customer subnet for admin access.
- Private S3-compatible store or mounted NFS for model artifacts (airgap-friendly).

Minimum deliverables for initial handoff (MVP):
1) Network diagram (customer-owned) with CIDRs and subnet mapping.
2) Terraform plan that: creates required subnets, route tables, security groups (restrictive by default), and a bastion instance.
3) Acceptance test script (curl/wget + short smoke checks) and a simple latency/curl checklist.
4) Signed network access agreement and IP allowlist (if control plane will talk to customer endpoints).
5) Rollback plan and upgrade window request (owner, time, contact).

Pre-handoff checklist (what we ask the customer):
- Confirm cloud provider and VPC CIDR(s)
- Provide KMS/HSM integration point or encryption policy
- Identify routing egress requirements (eg. to telemetry, registry, or KMS)
- Provide a primary contact and scheduled maintenance/upgrade windows
- Confirm whether models should be stored on object storage or local NFS (airgap)

Quick Terraform module guidance (patterns):
- Use redwood-private/vpc-lite module (internal) as the baseline. The module exposes variables:
  - customer_cidr (string)
  - public_subnet_cidrs (list)
  - private_subnet_cidrs (list)
  - bastion_instance_type (string)
  - allowlist_control_plane_ips (list)
- Recommended defaults: minimal open ports, only SSH from bastion, only TLS/GRPC from control plane allowlist, egress via NAT for outbound model pulls.
- Example tfvars snippet (paste into customer-facing snippet):
  customer_cidr = "10.250.0.0/16"
  public_subnet_cidrs = ["10.250.0.0/24"]
  private_subnet_cidrs = ["10.250.1.0/24"]
  bastion_instance_type = "t3.medium"
  allowlist_control_plane_ips = ["35.245.10.42/32"]

Notes on modules and diffs:
- Keep VPC module idempotent: changes to subnet sizes or removal should be gated behind explicit migration tickets.
- Tag every resource with customer-id and onboarding-ticket to make cost attribution and cleanup straightforward.
- Where possible use provider-agnostic constructs in our shared modules; add cloud-specific overlays for provider peculiarities (eg. GCP reserved ranges).

Acceptance tests (smoke):
- From bastion, verify connectivity to internal service endpoints (port checks):
  - tcp check 8080 (api)
  - tcp check 50051 (grpc)
- Minimal health endpoint curl:
  curl -sS --fail --connect-timeout 5 https://10.250.1.12:8080/healthz
- Model pull test (if permitted): attempt to pull a small model artifact from registry into node via the configured storage endpoint (or simulate via curl to object store).
- Latency sanity: sample inference 3x p50 < 120ms on baseline tiny model; capture in onboarding ticket.

Upgrade/patch plan (first-90-days recommendation):
- Week 0 (handoff): baseline deploy, acceptance tests, and security review signoff.
- Week 2: small patch window for tf module bugfixes and parameter tweaks (non-disruptive).
- Week 6: first non-trivial rollout (eg. config change or minor runtime bump) in canary with 10% traffic -> monitor errors/latency.
- Week 12: evaluate metrics and propose long-term autoscaling and quantization recommendations.

Rollback criteria and playbook:
- Immediate rollback if: repeated 5xx > 3% over 5 minutes, or p50 increased > 2x baseline for core route.
- Rollback steps: revert terraform change via branch-rollback (do not manually edit SGs unless emergency), redeploy last-green tf state, and notify customer.
- Post-rollback: attach debug trace, packet captures, and timeline to the incident ticket.

Security and compliance notes (regulatory customers):
- Use dedicated KMS keys per tenancy where required.
- Enable audit logs delivery to customer-managed logging collector (stackdriver/CloudWatch/Elk) with retention policy aligned to legal needs.
- For airgapped customers, exchange model artifacts via signed tarball and checksum; verify signatures during bootstrap.

Troubleshooting quick hits (for field engineers):
- No control plane connectivity: check allowlist and mTLS certs (control-plane cert expiry common gotcha).
- Model pull failures: check object store endpoint DNS, firewall egress, and time sync (expired signatures).
- Slow inference: confirm instance type and check that quantization flags are enabled and batching config is tuned.

Sign-off checklist (to close onboarding ticket):
- [ ] Customer confirms successful acceptance tests
- [ ] Network diagram imported to repo (network-diagrams/customer-<id>.png)
- [ ] TF plan applied with tagged resources
- [ ] Security review completed and KMS/HSM keys configured
- [ ] On-call escalation path shared with customer

Open questions / TODOs (items to resolve before finalizing playbook):
- Decide canonical pattern for control-plane connectivity: allowlist vs. managed reverse-proxy tunnel (security team preference?) -> action: schedule sync with @security (INF-4823).
- Standardize minimal instance types for GPU pools across cloud providers (cost/latency tradeoffs) -> add to product backlog.
- Add step-by-step for airgapped model ingestion (we currently have separate notes; consolidate into this doc).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a quick 'customer-facing one pager' stripped of operational internals that product/AE can hand to customers during sales handoff.
- Make a follow-up checklist for Dedicated vs. Hosted control plane differences.

References and useful links:
- Confluence: VPC Reference Patterns (linked above)
- GitHub: terraform-modules PR #127 (contains vpc-lite module)
- Jira: INF-4823 (control-plane connectivity decisions)

If you are taking ownership of the next pass: update the module names to align with the new naming convention (redwood-private/vpc-lite -> redwood-infra/vpc-tenant), and convert the acceptance tests into a small Go-based smoke runner that can be executed from CI and the bastion.

End of draft.
